#Goal
Assess the relationship between contact and the integration locations in the nested transposon hopping experiment. 
This script contains uses all the filtering relevant for the manuscript.
We discovered there is a mild saturation of unique integration sites close to the LP, so we switched from 'fraction of integration' to 'fraction of mapping reads', where we assume that the number of unique mapping reads is a better proxy of integration events.

# Correlate with hopping

## 25kb bin size
Need to 'fill in' all the bins that have 0 contact. The 4C bins are on round numbers of 5000. So I need to start by finding the bin border close to the LP.
Then make a tibble with all possible bins +-2Mb from LP

```{r}
all_bin_borders_tib_25kb = tib_PB_ints_sel %>%
  mutate(binwidth = 25000) %>%
  mutate(bin_border_at_LP = floor(start/binwidth)*binwidth,
         first_bin_border = bin_border_at_LP-2E6,
         last_bin_border =  bin_border_at_LP+2E6 + binwidth) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(bin = list(seq(first_bin_border, last_bin_border, by = binwidth))) %>%
  unnest(bin) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::rename(start_bin = bin) %>%
  mutate(end_bin = start_bin + binwidth,
         mid_bin = start_bin + binwidth/2,
         dist_from_PB = mid_bin - start,
         chromosome = str_remove(chr, "chr"))

all_bin_borders_tib_ls_25kb = all_bin_borders_tib_25kb %>%
  group_by(parental_clone) %>%
  group_split()

names(all_bin_borders_tib_ls_25kb) = c("WT78", "WT79", "WT83")
```

Link to SB read count
```{r}

SB_ints_by_contact_ls_25kb = lapply(c("WT78", "WT79", "WT83"), function(cl){
  intervals_4c_tib =  all_bin_borders_tib_ls_25kb[[cl]] %>%
    mutate(rownr = row_number())
  
  intervals_4c = intervals_4c_tib %>%
    select(chr, start_bin, end_bin, parental_clone) %>%
    dplyr::rename(start = start_bin, end = end_bin) %>%
    GRanges()
  
  ints_in_cl = SB_linked_tib %>% 
    uncount(read_count) %>% #count individual reads instead of integrations!
    filter(parental_clone == cl) %>%
    select(chr, start, end) %>%
    GRanges()
  
  N_SB_reads_per_interval = findOverlaps(intervals_4c, ints_in_cl, ignore.strand = T) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    group_by(queryHits) %>%
    summarize(N_SB_reads = n())
  
  intervals_4c_tib %>%
    left_join(N_SB_reads_per_interval, join_by(rownr == queryHits)) %>%
    mutate(N_SB_reads = replace_na(N_SB_reads, 0))
})

SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb = bind_rows(SB_ints_by_contact_ls_25kb) %>%
  left_join(virt_4C_tib_25kb_sel) %>%
  mutate(contact = na.replace(contact, 0))

```
25kb bins give no 0 contact, so that is nice.


##25kb bin, no psuedocounts
The psuedocounting is a bit risky: the amount of 0 bins depends on the hopping efficiency (and the bin size), which can depend on chromatin context. 
It is safer to just remove all zero bins and only look at the correlation in those regions where there is measurable contact and hopping


### summary of spearman cor

All distance, spearman correlation
```{r 4D_spearman_cor_per_LP_boxplot_close}
correlation_test_per_LP_spear_25kb = SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb %>%
  mutate(dist_from_LP = abs(mid_bin - start)) %>%
  filter(contact > 0 & N_SB_reads > 0) %>%
  filter(dist_from_LP <= 0.5E6) %>%
  group_by(LP_name) %>%
  summarize(cor_contact = cor.test(log10(N_SB_reads), log10(contact), method = 'spearman')$estimate,
            pval_contact = cor.test(log10(N_SB_reads), log10(contact), method = 'spearman')$p.val,
            cor_dist = cor.test(log10(N_SB_reads), log10(dist_from_LP), method = 'spearman')$estimate,
            pval_dist = cor.test(log10(N_SB_reads), log10(dist_from_LP), method = 'spearman')$p.val,,
            cor_contact_to_dist = cor.test(log10(dist_from_LP), log10(contact), method = 'spearman')$estimate)

set.seed(1234)
correlation_test_per_LP_spear_25kb %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c('LP_name', 'cor_contact_to_dist'),
               names_to = c(".value", "type"),
               names_pattern = "(cor|pval)_(contact|dist)") %>%
  ggplot( aes(x = type, y = abs(cor))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, aes(col = abs(cor_contact_to_dist))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab('correlation with...')+
  ylab('absolute spearman correlation') +
  scale_color_viridis_c() 

```
Note: difference between dist and contact only occurs when you filter for local (< 0.5 Mb), otherwise dist and contact are very similar.

# Effect chromatin launch site

On 25kb bins. This is slightly different form the analysis below, because here I use the actual chromatin at the 2kb surrounding the LP (as used in figure 2 for the transposition efficiency), while below (on the 10kb analysis) I use the whole 10kb bin with the LP in it (those 10kb bins are also not centered on the LP). 


```{r S5F_contact_correlation_by_LP_chromatin, fig.width = 15}

library(ggnewscale)
SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb_norm = SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb_2 %>%
  filter(contact > 0 & fract_SB_reads > 0 ) %>%
  mutate(log10_fract_reads = log10(fract_SB_reads),
         log10_contact = log10(contact))

contact_slope_tib_25kb_LPchrom_binary  = PB_context_tib_filt_hopef %>% 
  filter(window_size == 2000) %>%
  mutate(LP_feature_state = case_when(zscore>0 ~ 'high',
                                   .default = 'low')) %>%
  left_join(SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb_norm, relationship = 'many-to-many') #for each LP, multiple LP chromatin features & multiple contact bins
  
#colors
colscale_chrom_bins_line =  scale_colour_manual(values = c(low = 'grey30', high = 'darkorchid4'), aesthetics = c('col', 'fill'))
colscale_chrom_bins_points =  scale_colour_manual(values = c(low = 'grey60', high = 'orchid'), aesthetics = c('col'))

tib_for_plot_LP_chrom_state_25kb =
  contact_slope_tib_25kb_LPchrom_binary %>%
  filter(!feature %in% c("TTseq_fw", "TTseq_rv", "input_1", "input_2")) %>%
  slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = F) #randomly shuffle rows, to get random dataponts on top in overplotting

N_LPs_per_group = contact_slope_tib_25kb_LPchrom_binary %>%
  filter(!feature %in% c("TTseq_fw", "TTseq_rv", "input_1", "input_2")) %>%
  dplyr::select(LP_name, feature, LP_feature_state) %>% 
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(feature, LP_feature_state) %>% 
  summarize(N = n()) %>%
  mutate(y_pos = case_when(LP_feature_state == "high" ~ 10^-3 ,
                           .default = c(10^-3.5))) 

ggplot(tib_for_plot_LP_chrom_state_25kb, aes(x = contact, y = fract_SB_reads, col = LP_feature_state)) +
  facet_wrap(~feature) +
  #plot points
  ggrastr::rasterise( geom_point( alpha = 0.1, stroke = NA), dpi = 900) +
 
  colscale_chrom_bins_points +
  
  #plot lines, with a new  color scale
  new_scale_color() +
  colscale_chrom_bins_line +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', aes(col = LP_feature_state)) +
  
  #add text annotations
  # stat_regline_equation(aes(col = LP_feature_state))+
  geom_text( aes(x = 10^3, y =y_pos, #bottom right corner
                 label = paste0("n = ", N),
                 col = LP_feature_state),
             data = N_LPs_per_group,
             )+
  
  #layout
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number())+
  ylab('fraction of SB reads per bin') +
  theme_bw()+
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) 
```

# Effect chromatin integration site

## contact vs integration on 10kb bins
I would like to compare the density of integrations (N ints per bin) with the chromatin state at that bin, corrected for contact. 
I will first try this with the 10kb bins. Correlation with contact is okay at 10kb resolution and it gives a bit more relevant bins to work with than the 25kb binning.

```{r}
all_bin_borders_tib_10kb = tib_PB_ints_sel %>%
  mutate(binwidth = 10000) %>%
  mutate(bin_border_at_LP = floor(start/binwidth)*binwidth,
         first_bin_border = bin_border_at_LP-2E6,
         last_bin_border =  bin_border_at_LP+2E6 + binwidth) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(bin = list(seq(first_bin_border, last_bin_border, by = binwidth))) %>%
  unnest(bin) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::rename(start_bin = bin) %>%
  mutate(end_bin = start_bin + binwidth,
         mid_bin = start_bin + binwidth/2,
         dist_from_PB = mid_bin - start,
         chromosome = str_remove(chr, "chr")) 

all_bin_borders_tib_ls_10kb = all_bin_borders_tib_10kb %>%
  group_by(parental_clone) %>%
  group_split()

names(all_bin_borders_tib_ls_10kb) = c("WT78", "WT79", "WT83")
```

Link to SB counts
```{r}

SB_ints_by_contact_ls_10kb = lapply(c("WT78", "WT79", "WT83"), function(cl){
  intervals_4c_tib =  all_bin_borders_tib_ls_10kb[[cl]] %>%
    mutate(rownr = row_number())
  
  intervals_4c = intervals_4c_tib %>%
    select(chr, start_bin, end_bin, parental_clone) %>%
    dplyr::rename(start = start_bin, end = end_bin) %>%
    GRanges()
  
  ints_in_cl = SB_linked_tib %>% 
    uncount(read_count) %>% #count individual reads instead of integrations!
    filter(parental_clone == cl) %>%
    select(chr, start, end) %>%
    GRanges()
  
  N_SB_reads_per_interval = findOverlaps(intervals_4c, ints_in_cl, ignore.strand = T) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    group_by(queryHits) %>%
    summarize(N_SB_reads = n())
  
  intervals_4c_tib %>%
    left_join(N_SB_reads_per_interval, join_by(rownr == queryHits)) %>%
    mutate(N_SB_reads = replace_na(N_SB_reads, 0))
})

SB_ints_by_contact_tib_10kb = bind_rows(SB_ints_by_contact_ls_10kb) %>%
  left_join(virt_4C_tib_10kb_sel) %>%
  mutate(contact = na.replace(contact, 0)) %>%
  group_by(LP_name) %>%
  mutate(SB_reads_total = sum(N_SB_reads),
         fract_SB_reads = N_SB_reads / SB_reads_total
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


```

As a sanity check, do we get similar results as for the 25kb bins above?
```{r }

SB_ints_by_contact_tib_10kb %>%
  filter(contact > 0 & N_SB_reads > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = contact, y = fract_SB_reads)) +
  stat_cor(label.y.npc = 'top', vjust = 1, method = 'spearman') +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)+
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm') +
  stat_regline_equation(label.y.npc = 0.8)+
  scale_x_log10()+
  scale_y_log10()+ 
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position =  'none') +
  ylab('fraction of SB reads per bin')

```
Yes, the slope is still 0.78, so analysis on 10kb bins gives a similar relationship as on 25kb bins.

## link to contact
make a wide tibble that has the correct boundaries (matching the contact tibble)
```{r}
chrom_bins_filt_forlink= chrom_bins_filt %>%
  distinct() %>% #there are a few duplicate bins, from LPs (in different clones) that are <4 Mb apart
  dplyr::rename(start_bin = start_interval) %>%
  mutate(end_bin = end_interval + 1) %>% #to make it match the bins in the microC object
  dplyr::select(-end_interval)

chrom_bins_filt_forlink_wide = chrom_bins_filt_forlink %>%
  select(chr, start_bin, end_bin, feature, zscore) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = zscore)

SB_ints_by_contact_tib_10kb_chrom = SB_ints_by_contact_tib_10kb %>%
  left_join(chrom_bins_filt_forlink_wide)

```


## plot binarized (high/low)

Calculate systematically for each mark
```{r }

library(ggh4x)

#binarize all features
SB_ints_by_contact_tib_10kb_chrom_binary = SB_ints_by_contact_tib_10kb_chrom %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = unique(chrom_bins_filt$feature),
               names_to = 'feature',
               values_to = 'zscore') %>%
    filter(contact >0 & N_SB_reads >0 & !is.na(zscore)) %>% #NAs occur in the chrom tibble when bins were filtered out
  mutate(feature_state = case_when(zscore>0 ~ 'high',
                                   .default = 'low')) %>%
  group_by(LP_name, feature) %>%
  mutate(fract_high = sum(feature_state == 'high')/length(feature_state)) 

#collect features at LP
feature_states_LP = SB_ints_by_contact_tib_10kb_chrom_binary %>%
  filter(bin_border_at_LP == start_bin) %>%
  select(parental_clone, LP_name, feature, feature_state) %>%
  dplyr::rename(LP_feature_state = feature_state)
```
